newsitem.title: USA: India moves missiles near Pakistani border-report.
newsitem.headline: India moves missiles near Pakistani border-report.

text.p: India's military forces recently moved some medium-range ballistic missiles to a prospective launch site near the Pakistani border, the Washington Post reported in Tuesday editions.
Quoting U.S. officials, the newspaper said India's actions had raised fresh concerns that the two enemies had entered a provocative phase in their longstanding arms race.
The missiles, called Prithvis, were capable of carrying conventional but not nuclear warheads.

The officials told the newspaper that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that fewer than a dozen of the missiles were now located near the city of Jullundur in the state of Punjab in northwest India.

Some intelligence officials described the movement of the missiles as the first operational deployment of the Prithvi since its development began over a decade ago. Other officials said it was unclear if all the equipment needed to launch the missiles had also been moved to the northwest border.
